name: Acorn Master Compact Mouse Driver (PMFS)
description: An annotated disassembly of PMFS, the pointer and mouse driver on the Acorn BBC Master Compact Welcome disc. PMFS is a 65C02 sideways ROM image, loaded into sideways RAM, that moves a software pointer from a quadrature mouse or trackerball, an analogue or digital joystick, or the cursor keys, and reports its position through ADVAL. MOS 5 has no mouse support of its own, so PMFS is the Master Compact's mouse driver, and the interface it presents is the one Welcome-era software expects. PMFS is (C) 1986 PMF, identified as Paul Fellows; the annotations and disassembly scripts here are (C) 2026 Acornaeology.

analyses.label: The Master Compact pointer driver interface: a specification
analyses.note: A formal definition of the interface PMFS presents to software (star commands, ADVAL(5)-(9), OSBYTE &A3,&F3, buttons as keys, coordinates and the pointer display), written so that drivers for other pointing hardware can be compatible with it, with PMFS's defects listed separately.

analyses.label: How PMFS works
analyses.note: The driver's internal design: running from sideways RAM with its workspace in its own bank, reaching BYTEV and IRQ1V through the Master's extended vectors, the workspace exchange, reading a quadrature mouse through the User VIA, and drawing a software pointer with pre-shifted images.

references.label: Tom Seddon's annotated disassembly of the Master MOS
references.note: The Master Compact's MOS 5.00, whose service calls, extended vectors, joystick handling and *SRLOAD PMFS relies on.

references.label: David Atherton, Master Operating System: A Dabhand Guide (Dabs Press, 1987), remade edition
references.note: Reserves &0D92-&0D9E for a trackerball or other input device (p205), where PMFS keeps its saved vectors and IRQ1V routine, and allows a mouse driver to use it (p79).

references.label: The Master Compact Welcome disc image (acorn.huininga.nl)
references.note: Disc title "Welcome 1.03C Iss4". Byte-identical to the copy kept in this repository, from which the PMFS ROM image is extracted.

references.label: VectorEyes's flux capture of a Master Compact Welcome disc
references.note: A capture of a physical "Welcome, Application and Utilities" disc titled "Welcome 1.03C Iss4". Every file on it, PMFS included, is identical to the image used here, which also holds three files written by the Welcome desktop.

references.label: Econet Level 4 File Server supplementary discs, issues 1 and 2
references.note: Their $.Comp_Wel directory holds the later 6 KB build of PMFS 136 (MD5 8826f28b3575e9481944528ebf09893c), not disassembled here.

references.label: PMFS in the ROM Library
references.note: The ROM Library's entry for PMFS, with the 6 KB and 8 KB builds and links to Acorn User articles of December 1986 and April 1987.

references.label: Paul Fellows at Binary Dinosaurs
references.note: Paul Fellows ran Acornsoft's languages group and led the team that wrote Arthur. He was identified as the PMF of PMFS's copyright string by @acheton1984.

references.label: Marconi trackerball ROM in the ROM Library
references.note: An earlier Acorn pointer driver, (C) Acorn 1985, supplied with the Marconi trackerball.

references.label: Domesday VFS ROMs in the ROM Library
references.note: The Video Filing System of the Domesday (Master AIV) system, (C) 1986 Acorn. Master Operating System: A Dabhand Guide (p79) notes that the Master AIV system includes code to drive the Marconi trackerball.
